solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

parts.note: to con is to study or pore over
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A student reads poems and discusses them.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to hold a conversation, a formal verb for chatting.

clue.text: Old poet in pandemic losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: Covid was the pandemic disease of 2020

explanation.surface: A classical poet caught up in a modern pandemic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was the Roman poet who wrote the Metamorphoses, so he is an ancient writer of verse.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: perched at the brink of something, ready to tip over

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second, literal meaning: an object sitting at the very rim of a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an anxious person, while literally it places an object right at a precipice where it may topple.

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in pros and cons
a pup is one young animal in a litter

explanation.surface: Helping one of a newborn litter of puppies.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop up is to hold upright or bolster, a phrasal verb meaning to sustain.

clue.text: Asks how paper may be folded

definitions.meaning: second meaning, split as two words: a quire is a set of sheets folded together

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, IN QUIRES: a quire is a bundle of folded sheets of paper, traditionally 24 or 25.
explanation.definitionFit: Inquires is the American-leaning spelling of enquires, a verb meaning seeks information.

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Something placed on a table with its front showing, like a playing card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face up' looks like how something was put down; 'face' is a clock face and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past tense of lay, meaning set or placed down on a surface.

indicators.note: to change something is to alter its arrangement, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tourist anxiously swaps something bought abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A souvenir is a memento typically bought while travelling, the classic trinket brought home from a trip.

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked theatre
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Japanese play whose story concerns a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah built and sailed the ark in Genesis, so he is the Bible's best-known vessel captain.

clue.text: Leave, and need regularly to have escaped

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone must go, and needs to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of LEAVE AND NEED give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to dodge or get away from, so evaded is a synonym of escaped.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: Ezra ..., the American modernist poet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat poet' suggests Ginsberg or Kerouac; the question mark warns that the two words are split.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound is to hit hard, and Ezra Pound was a major twentieth-century writer of verse.

clue.text: Antelope hung back to avoid horse

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from right to left
to avoid something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A wild antelope holds back so as to keep away from a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is drug slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnu, or wildebeest, is a large African antelope.

clue.text: Born rascal that goes on foot

parts.note: b. is the abbreviation for born
a rogue is a rascal

explanation.surface: A natural scoundrel who travels on foot, like a vagabond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes on foot' suggests walking; in fact it is something worn there.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a sturdy leather shoe with decorative perforations, an item worn on the foot.

clue.text: Complained malingering finally has been found out

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of malingering
to be rumbled is British slang for to be found out

explanation.surface: A shirker grumbles after their skiving is discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumbled is British informal for discovered or seen through.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble is to moan or whine, so grumbled is a synonym of complained.

indicators.note: is in means one word sits inside the other

parts.note: pure means perfect, unblemished
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A location in the ideal shade, as if a garden spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Purple is a colour, and shade is a common word for a colour or tint.

clue.text: Connective tissue: mangle it when injured

indicators.note: something injured is damaged out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports injury: the tissue in a joint gets mangled.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is a band of fibrous tissue connecting bones at a joint.

indicators.note: remarkable hints at something out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Northern Ireland achieves an astonishing outcome, perhaps in a match or election.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': Ulster is remarkable. Ulster is a name for Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A result is the consequence or final score of something, a synonym of outcome.

indicators.note: around means one word encloses the other

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Fish swimming about a river's course.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch, which is a kind of channel cut in the ground.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a banner, especially one flown by a ship
second meaning: a former lowest commissioned infantry rank, who carried the colours

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag officer' is a real naval rank (admiral), which pulls the words together; split them.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a naval flag, and historically also the junior officer who bore the regiment's standard.

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a boss is a manager

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be promoted over their manager.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'above' simply places the first piece before the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to raise a design in relief on a surface, so it means to make something raised.

clue.text: Memory rocky at first in the morning

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of rocky
a.m. marks the hours in the morning

explanation.surface: Someone's recall is shaky first thing in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' belongs with 'the morning': together they mean a.m., not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: RAM, random-access memory, is the working memory of a computer.

clue.text: Female competent to produce old wives' tale

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
able means competent

explanation.surface: A capable woman tells a piece of folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a traditional made-up story, and an old wives' tale is a fanciful popular belief or yarn.

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Instructions to pick up a good fish, as at a market.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel is to touch or finger something, a synonym of the verb handle.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: turn into something else
second meaning: look good on, as a colour suits someone

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests putting on a suit; 'into' belongs with 'Change'.
explanation.definitionFit: To become is to grow into a new state, and also to flatter or look right on someone.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... revolver, a firearm
second meaning: a young male horse

explanation.walkthrough: The surface grimly asks what gun to put down a horse with; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Colt is a famous make of revolver, and a colt is also a young male equine.

clue.text: Only a small body of water

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a lake or pond, as in English place names

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, 'only a little water'; split after 'Only'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere as an adjective means nothing more than, and as a noun is an old word for a lake or pond.

clue.text: Shedding outside layer, initially making a defensive move

indicators.note: outside means one word goes around the other

parts.note: casting means shedding, as a snake casts its skin

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of layer

explanation.surface: A creature sheds its outer skin as a means of protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside layer' reads as skin, but 'outside' is the container signal and 'layer' supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Castling is the chess move where king and rook switch places, typically to tuck the king safely away.
